sources.note: Nothing on Pisabo; states 'no linguistic data is available, and it is reported to be mutually intelligible with Matses' (citing Fleck 2013 and Ethnologue 18 for 600 speakers).

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan Languages and Linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History 99. New York: AMNH. hdl 2246/6448.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Pisabo is listed in Table 2 (p. 13) 'Tentative Classification of Possibly Panoan Languages/Dialects Lacking Linguistic Data', I. Mayoruna branch: 'Pisabo – Mayoruna subtribe (Grubb, 1927: 83)'; p. 10: 'Table 2 provides a list of ethnonyms/language names that have been claimed to be Panoan, but for which no linguistic data are available.' Index p. 86: 'Pisabo (T2: I) – var: Pisabu, Pisahua, Pissabo.'; p. 108: 'Pisabo – Gálvez R (lb af Javari R), Peru. (Grubb, 1927: 83).'

sources.citation: Grubb, Kenneth G. 1927. The Lowland Indians of Amazonia: a survey of the location and religious condition of the Indians of Colombia, Venezuela, the Guianas, Ecuador, Peru, Brazil and Bolivia. London: World Dominion Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; the sole primary mention of the group is ethnographic, p. 83: 'As very small sub-tribes [of the Mayoruna] we mention the Marubo and the Pisabu on the River Galvez.' plus a tribe list p. 132 ('Mayoruna (Mayo). Marubo, Pisabu.') and index 'Pisabu, 83'. No words, no language data.

sources.note: Nothing; classification Unattested > Pano-Tacanan (Unattested); comment: 'E16..E28 has an entry for Pisabo [pig]. But Pisabo is unattested (Fleck 2013) and cannot be asserted to have been a separate language.' Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist (Uriarte 1976, a population overview).

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2003. A grammar of Matses. PhD dissertation, Rice University (1257 pp.), ch. on phonology incl. stress.

sources.note: Not a Pisabo source, but if Pisabo was (as reported) a Matses/Mayoruna-branch variety mutually intelligible with Matses, the Matses stress description (mats1244) is the nearest proxy; relevant only if the catalog decides to fold pisa1244 into Matses rather than leave it unattested.
